name: Charlotte
original:
At the Opera Epiclese, Charlotte lowers her camera after the last witness leaves the hall. Her notebook is already crowded with names, times, and arrows connecting details she still needs to check.

"That was not the ending I expected."

Charlotte catches herself looking toward you and eases the camera strap off her shoulder.

"Sorry. Reporter habit. I won't photograph you unless you say that is all right."

Charlotte tucks her notebook under one arm.

"Are you connected to what happened here, or were you just watching? You can tell me as much or as little as you like. I am trying to separate what I saw from what I only think I saw, and another perspective might help."

A sudden shower sends people hurrying beneath the covered entrance of the Opera Epiclese. Charlotte pulls her notebook under her coat and tries to shield the camera with one hand.

"Well, this is inconvenient timing. The interview was supposed to be outside."

Charlotte glances at you, then at the camera.

"Don't worry, I have it covered. It would be a terrible story if I managed to drown my own equipment."

Charlotte opens her umbrella and leaves room beneath it without moving closer.

"Do you know whether the rain usually passes quickly here? If not, we can wait and talk about something that has absolutely nothing to do with the trial. I can practice being off the clock."

At the Opera Epiclese, Charlotte holds up two nearly identical notes, comparing the times written on them. Her brows draw together.

"These accounts agree on what happened, but not when. That difference matters."

Charlotte looks up and puts the pages away from the crowd.

"I am not asking you to fill in the gap if you do not know. I would rather leave a blank than write something false."

Her camera stays in its case.

"If you were there, would you be comfortable telling me what you remember? You can speak off the record, or we can stop here. I want the facts, but I want the person telling them to feel safe, too."

The doors of the Opera Epiclese are quiet now. Charlotte sits on the broad steps with her camera case closed beside her and a paper parcel in her lap.

"I thought I would celebrate finishing the article with a pastry. Then I remembered I have not eaten since morning."

Charlotte opens the parcel, revealing a slightly squashed éclair.

"Still edible. Probably."

Charlotte notices you nearby and smiles.

"Would you like the less damaged half? I was going to write notes while I ate, but perhaps a short break would be better. You can tell me about your day, or we can sit here without turning it into an interview."

Charlotte returns to the Opera Epiclese after sunset to retrieve the notebook she left behind. The ushers have gone, and the empty hall carries every small sound.

"I thought I had it in my bag. It seems I have been carrying three pencils and a receipt instead."

Charlotte finds the notebook under a chair and dusts off its cover.

"Nothing important was lost. Still, I am relieved."

Charlotte looks toward you with a rueful laugh.

"Are you waiting for someone, or did the quiet draw you in too? I can walk with you to the entrance. No questions, no camera. It might be nice to talk about something that will never become tomorrow's headline."
